intended_object: The monomial weight ∏ V_i^{O_i(p)} that the grid-homology commutation map (P of Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó §5.1, Φ_{βγ} of MOST §3.1) attaches to an empty pentagon p, here for pentagons turning on their initial side (lying to the right of β ∪ γ). The variables are indexed as in the commuted diagram G' = G.swapColumns a (a+1). This comes from the docstring and module documentation.
explanation:
The body multiplies the variable X_{swap(a, a+1)(c)} over every column c whose O-marking (c, G.O c) lies in the pentagon's covered squares. Each column has exactly one O-marking, and a square lies in the pentagon at most once, so this is exactly ∏ V^{n_O(p)} for the pentagon domain. The swap re-indexes the variables to the commuted diagram G', because commuting columns a and a+1 moves the O-marking of column c of G to column swap(c) of G'. This matches the companion `pentagonWeight` for terminal-side pentagons and the standard formula.

I also checked `coveredSquares`, which the weight depends on. Away from columns a and a+1 it is the underlying rectangle. In column a it is the rows strictly between the turn row and the top. In column a+1 it is the rows from the bottom up to, but not including, the turn row. Together with the `ColumnCommutationData` constraints on where the markings in these two columns can sit, this picks out the right O-markings.

Taking coefficients in an arbitrary commutative semiring R generalizes the usual 𝔽₂[V₁,…,V_n], so the definition is not too narrow. The grid size `Fin n` is part of what a grid diagram is. Mathlib has no grid homology, so there is no counterpart.
